The property owner, Raman (left), and contractor Anwar (right) of the building that collapsed in Central Delhi’s Paharganj, injuring 8 people on November 15 | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement
The Delhi police on Monday (November 17, 2026) apprehended the owner and contractor of an under-construction hotel in Paharganj and registered an FIR against them, a day after a portion of the building collapsed, injuring eight workers .
“The property owner Raman and a contractor Anwar have been apprehended and are being bound down,” Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said.
The accused were booked under Sections 290 (negligent conduct with respect to buildings), 125(a) (act endangering life or personal safety), 223(a) (disobedience of an order duly promulgated by a public servant) and 3(5) (common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said.
The incident occurred amid restrictions on dust-generating outdoor construction activities imposed to curb air pollution under the Graded Response Action Plan. However, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) maintained that construction was not underway at the time of the incident.
“Construction was not ongoing. They were removing the shuttering. And that is not construction,” said MCD Deputy Commissioner Vinod Atri.
An MCD inspection report, accessed by The Hindu , stated that the building at Property No. 3992–3993 in Kaseruwalan, Paharganj, was being constructed under a sanctioned building plan issued on June 4, 2024. No unauthorised construction was found at the property during the inspection, it said.
According to the report, a portion of a newly constructed lintel on the ground floor gave way while workers were removing its shuttering. It recorded five people as having sustained minor injuries and being shifted to Lady Hardinge Hospital, against the eight people whom the police said were taken to hospital for medico-legal examination.
The report stated that construction had been completed up to the basement and stilt floor, along with part of the upper ground floor. It did not establish the exact cause of the collapse.
The incident came 10 days after seven workers were killed when an “unauthorised” three-storey building under construction collapsed in Old Delhi’s Chawri Bazar on November 5.
The two incidents have raised questions about safety measures at construction sites and their enforcement. For workers, however, the risks extend beyond structural collapses. Inadequate protective equipment, long working hours and pressure to meet deadlines are among the problems they face.
